title: The Sum of the Values on the Way From the Root, With Changes

concept.title: Number the nodes in the order of a depth-first walk: a subtree is then one range, and a change of a node is a range addition
body: A rooted tree has a number written in every node. An operation **adds a number to the value of one node**, and a question asks for the **sum of the values of all the nodes on the way from the root down to a node `v`** (both ends included). For a path `1 - 2 - 3` with the values `5, 1, 4`, the sum to the node 3 is 10; after adding 10 to the node 2 it is 20. Walking up from `v` to the root costs O(depth) per question, which is O(n) on a long chain.

The *Euler tour* trick: number the nodes `0..n-1` in the order of a depth-first walk (preorder), `tin[v]`, and let `size[v]` be the number of nodes in the subtree of `v`. The subtree of `v` is exactly the range `tin[v] .. tin[v] + size[v] - 1`. Adding `x` to the value of `v` changes the root-path sum of **every node in the subtree of `v`** (and of no other node) by `x`. So the operation is a **range addition** on the positions of the subtree, and a question is a **point query** at `tin[v]`: the structure is the Fenwick tree for "range add, point query" (a tree of differences). Keep also the starting path sum `init[v] = init[parent] + value[v]`, computed once.

body.code:
order the nodes so that every parent comes before its children  (guaranteed by the input)
size[v]: add the size of every node to its parent, from the last node to the first
tin[v]: the first child gets the parent's tin + 1, the next gets the previous sibling's tin + size ...
init[v] = init[parent[v]] + value[v]

add x to the node v:   bit_add(t, tin[v] + 1, x);  bit_add(t, tin[v] + size[v] + 1, -x)
question for v:        init[v] + bit_sum(t, tin[v] + 1)

body: The numbering can be done without recursion because the parent of every node has a smaller number: process the nodes in increasing order, keeping for each node the next free position `nxt[parent]`. Everything is O((n + q) log n). The same Euler-tour numbering turns many tree questions (sums over subtrees, changes of subtrees) into questions about ranges.

statement: A rooted tree with `n` nodes (the root is the node 1, and the parent of every node has a smaller number) has a value in every node. Process `q` operations: type 1 `v x` adds `x` to the value of the node `v`; type 2 `v 0` asks for the sum of the values of all nodes on the path from the root to the node `v`. Print the answers to the questions on one line, in order.
inputFormat: The first line has `n` and `q`: the number of nodes and the number of operations.
The second line has `n` numbers: the parent of every node (0 for the root, which is the node 1; the parent of a node has a smaller number).
The third line has `n` numbers: the values of the nodes.

Each of the next `q` lines has three numbers `t`, `v` and `x`. If `t = 1`, add `x` to the value of the node `v` (`x` is the added number). If `t = 2`, print the sum of the values on the path from the root to the node `v` (`x` is 0).
outputFormat: Print one number for every operation of type 2, separated by spaces.

examples.note: The path 1 - 2 - 3 has the sum 5 + 1 + 4 = 10; after the addition 5 + 11 + 4 = 20: 10 20.

hints: Number the nodes in a depth-first order; a subtree is a range.
Adding to a node adds to the whole subtree range of root-path sums.
Use a Fenwick tree of differences for range add and point query, plus the initial path sums.

explanation: The nodes are numbered in depth-first order so that every subtree is a range; adding to a node is a range addition on its subtree in a Fenwick tree of differences, and the path sum of a node is its initial path sum plus the point value at its position.
solution.complexity: Time O((n + q) log n), space O(n).

code.python:
import sys
input = sys.stdin.readline

def bit_add(t, i, x):
    n = len(t) - 1
    while i <= n:
        t[i] += x
        i += i & -i

def bit_sum(t, i):
    s = 0
    while i > 0:
        s += t[i]
        i -= i & -i
    return s

n, q = map(int, input().split())
par = list(map(int, input().split()))
a = list(map(int, input().split()))
ops = [list(map(int, input().split())) for _ in range(q)]

sz = [1] * (n + 1)
for v in range(n, 1, -1):
    sz[par[v - 1]] += sz[v]
tin = [0] * (n + 1)
nxt = [0] * (n + 1)
nxt[1] = 1
init = [0] * (n + 1)
init[1] = a[0]
for v in range(2, n + 1):
    p = par[v - 1]
    tin[v] = nxt[p]
    nxt[p] += sz[v]
    nxt[v] = tin[v] + 1
    init[v] = init[p] + a[v - 1]
t = [0] * (n + 2)
out = []
for kind, v, x in ops:
    if kind == 1:
        bit_add(t, tin[v] + 1, x)
        bit_add(t, tin[v] + sz[v] + 1, -x)
    else:
        out.append(init[v] + bit_sum(t, tin[v] + 1))
print(*out)
